text: Let n denote the number of samples in the training set, where n is a positive integer.
The learning rate alpha controls the step size taken during each gradient update.
We denote by theta the vector of model parameters to be optimized.
Here, x_i is the i-th input feature vector and y_i is its corresponding label.
The loss function L measures the discrepancy between predictions and ground-truth labels.
Let G = (V, E) be a graph with vertex set V and edge set E.
The temperature T is a hyperparameter that scales the logits before the softmax.
We use sigma to denote the standard deviation of the Gaussian noise added to each pixel.
The matrix W represents the weights of the fully connected layer, and b is the bias term.
For each epoch t, the model parameters are updated using the accumulated gradients.
